no_target_yet.statement:
For the frames and state above, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S_\tau(x)+S_\omega(x)=D(c)$;
\item $\dim_\HH\mathcal Q=1$, $\norm{\tau_\alpha}=1$ for $\mu$-almost
every $\alpha$, and $\norm{\omega_\beta}=1$ for $\nu$-almost every $\beta$.
\end{enumerate}
Under either condition, $m=n=c=1$ and $S_\tau(x)=S_\omega(x)=0$.
Consequently every link in \eqref{eq:chain} is an equality.
For a fixed frame pair, such a state exists if and only if condition 2
holds and every $\tau_\alpha$ and every $\omega_\beta$ is nonzero,
including at null indices.

no_target_yet.statement:
For finite counting frames in a nonzero real or complex Banach space,
the mass and central lower entropy equalities in
\cite[Questions 1--2, Theorems 4--5, (5) and (7)]{K24}
occur exactly in dimension one, with all first-family functional
norms $m^{-1/r}$ and all second-family norms $n^{-1/r}$.

The strict positivity of the lower endpoint printed in those
theorems must be replaced by nonnegativity.

$R_N(z_1,\ldots,z_N)=(0,z_1,\ldots,z_{N-1})$.
With $w_\HH(R_N)=\sup_{\norm{z}=1}\abs{\ip{z}{R_Nz}}$, one has
\[

\]

no_target_yet.next_step: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.reason: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.statement:
Suppose $p:\Omega\to(0,1]$ and $q:\Delta\to(0,1]$ are measurable,
have integral one, and satisfy $p(\alpha)q(\beta)\le M$ at every pair
of indices, where $0<M\le1$. Then
\[
 \int-p\log p\,d\mu+\int-q\log q\,d\nu\ge-\log M.
\]
Equality holds precisely when there are $A,B\in(0,1]$ with $AB=M$
such that $p=A$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and $q=B$ $\nu$-almost everywhere.

no_target_yet.statement:
Suppose the two frame families have pointwise norm bounds
$0<a\le1$ and $0<b\le1$, respectively. On the common coefficient
domain,
\[
 S_\tau(x)+S_\omega(x)\ge-2\log\frac{ab+c}{2}.
\]
Equality holds exactly when $\dim_\HH\mathcal Q=1$,
$\norm{\tau_\alpha}=a$ almost everywhere, and
$\norm{\omega_\beta}=b$ almost everywhere.
Then $m=a^{-2}$, $n=b^{-2}$ and $c=ab$.
For $ab<1$ this strengthens the source's central lower bound strictly.
The same statement holds over $\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb C$.

no_target_yet.next_step: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.reason: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.statement:
Let $1\le r<\infty$ and let $\{f_\alpha\}$, $\{g_\beta\}$ be 1-bounded
continuous Parseval $r$-frames of linear functionals on a real or complex
Banach space $X$. Thus their norms are at most one, their coefficient
maps are measurable, and $\int\abs{f_\alpha(y)}^r\,d\mu=\norm{y}^r$,
with the analogous identity for $g$.
For a unit vector $u$ with all these coefficients nonzero, define
\[
 P(\alpha)=\abs{f_\alpha(u)}^r,\qquad
 Q(\beta)=\abs{g_\beta(u)}^r,\qquad
 C=\sup_{\norm{y}=1,\,\alpha,\beta}\abs{f_\alpha(y)g_\beta(y)}.
\]
Equality in the lower entropy bound
$\int-P\log P+\int-Q\log Q\ge-r\log C$
holds exactly when $P=A$ almost everywhere, $Q=B$ almost everywhere,
and $AB=C^r$ for constants $A,B>0$.
In particular both total masses are finite at equality.
The same criterion holds for the dual-space frames of
\cite[Theorem 2.12]{K23}, with coefficients
$f_\alpha(h)=h(\tau_\alpha)$ and $g_\beta(h)=h(\omega_\beta)$ on $X^*$.
For finite $m,n$, upper entropy equality with $\log(mn)$ holds
exactly when $P=1/m$ and $Q=1/n$ almost everywhere.
no_target_yet.title: Krishna's quaternionic Deutsch equality question and a short proof of Carvalho–Diogo–Mendes's shift consequence

no_target_yet.statement:
In the functional setting of Corollary~\ref{cor:functional}, assume
$X\ne\{0\}$ and $m,n<\infty$. Equality in the other inequality of
\cite[Theorems 2.8 and 2.12, (4)--(5)]{K23}, namely
\[
 (mn)^{-1/r}\le C,
\]
holds if and only if $\dim X=1$ and
\[
 \norm{f_\alpha}\le m^{-1/r},\quad
 \norm{g_\beta}\le n^{-1/r}\quad\hbox{at every index},
\]
with equality in each norm bound almost everywhere.
For the dual formulation, replace $X$ by $X^*$ and the functionals
by the corresponding evaluation maps. Every admissible state
then attains the functional lower entropy bound as well.
For arbitrary total masses and an admissible state, lower entropy
equality holds if and only if $m,n$ are finite and the same
dimension and norm conditions hold. For a fixed pair an admissible
equality state exists precisely when these conditions hold and
every functional is nonzero, including at null indices.
